name: cross_module_refs
description: Finds all requirements in one module that reference, depend on, or trace into requirements in another module. Covers both explicit edges (SATISFIES, DERIVES_FROM, REFINES, VERIFIES, CONFLICTS_WITH) and LLM-discovered ones (SEMANTICALLY_DEPENDS_ON, COMPLEMENTS, CONSTRAINS, POTENTIALLY_CONFLICTS), with the edge provenance surfaced per row. This is the canonical shape for 'how does FCC talk to PWR' interface-boundary questions, and the result is the exact list an integration engineer needs when redrawing a module boundary.
when_to_use: Fire this template when the user asks about connections between two specific modules. Typical phrasings: 'show all requirements in FCC that reference PWR', 'cross-module links between INS and NAV', 'what does CDL depend on in COMM', 'FCC to PWR boundary'. The user must name both a source module and a target module. Do not fire when the user is asking about a single module — use module_coverage or platform_requirements instead.

parameters.name: module_a
parameters.description: The source Module.name. Requirements from this module will appear on the left of each result row. Example values: 'FCC', 'INS', 'CDL'. Use the exact uppercase module code.

parameters.name: module_b
parameters.description: The target Module.name. Requirements from this module will appear on the right of each result row. Example values: 'PWR', 'NAV', 'COMM'. Use the exact uppercase module code.

cypher:
MATCH (a:Requirement)-[rel:SATISFIES|DERIVES_FROM|REFINES|VERIFIES|CONFLICTS_WITH|SEMANTICALLY_DEPENDS_ON|COMPLEMENTS|CONSTRAINS|POTENTIALLY_CONFLICTS]-(b:Requirement)
WHERE a.module = $module_a
  AND b.module = $module_b
RETURN DISTINCT
       a.id                                        AS source_id,
       a.heading                                   AS source_heading,
       a.summary                                   AS source_summary,
       type(rel)                                   AS relationship,
       coalesce(rel.discovery_method, 'explicit')  AS provenance,
       rel.confidence                              AS llm_confidence,
       b.id                                        AS target_id,
       b.heading                                   AS target_heading,
       b.summary                                   AS target_summary
ORDER BY provenance, source_id, target_id
notes: The match pattern is undirected (no arrow) so it catches edges in both orientations — an FCC requirement that SATISFIES a PWR one and a PWR requirement that CONSTRAINS an FCC one both appear, with the source/target columns oriented to the user's query. Ordering by provenance puts explicit edges before LLM-discovered ones so the reader sees the auditable links first. Confidence column is only populated on LLM edges; it is null for explicit ones, which is what the agent should render as a blank cell.
